open_points.subject: ProjectValidationResult status consistency
open_points.text: `status: str | None`, `is_active: bool` ... Portal mutation policy uses only `is_active` for the grant and assignment operations of access management and only `status` (`active` or not) in the project guard
open_points.question: What relationship must hold between `status` and `is_active`, and what is the authoritative lifecycle fact if they disagree?
options: Require `is_active` to be true exactly when `status` is `active`.
Permit disagreement and let access-management creation use `is_active` while project operations use `status`.
Treat a disagreement as an invalid Registry result.

witness.initial: Registry returns a validation result for project P with `exists=true`, `status="archived"`, `is_active=true`, and no failure.
events: An administrator attempts to assign an operator to P.
The operator attempts a guarded project operation on P.
outcomes: The assignment succeeds because it uses `is_active`, but the guarded operation treats P as archived.
The validation result is rejected or normalized, so the assignment does not succeed.
witness.observer: The administrator and operator see whether the assignment exists and whether it grants usable access.

open_points.subject: Registry checks for grant and assignment revocation
open_points.text: M17 says, “Portal mutation policy uses only `is_active` for the grant and assignment operations of access management”; R0-24 says, “Revoking an existing viewer grant, staff assignment or producer grant does not consult the Registry and succeeds for an archived project, also while the Registry is unavailable.”
open_points.question: Does “grant and assignment operations” mean only creation, or does M17 require an `is_active` check for revocation too?
options: Only creation uses `is_active`; revocation never consults Registry.
Both creation and revocation use `is_active`, so revocation can be refused when inactive or unavailable.
open_points.default_guess: Limit the M17 statement to creation; preserve R0-24 revocation behavior.

witness.initial: Project P is archived and has an active staff assignment.
outcomes: R0-24: revocation succeeds without a Registry read.
The broad M17 wording: revocation requires `is_active`, so it cannot succeed without validation.
witness.observer: The administrator and the formerly assigned staff member see whether access was revoked.

open_points.subject: Actor provenance for failed staff login
open_points.text: “a `staff.login_failed` record carries none” together with `actor_kind: ActorKind (staff | viewer | service | system)` and `actor_id: UUID | None` `[required unless system]`
open_points.question: Who is the actor of `staff.login_failed` when the submitted email matches no StaffAccount, and must that failed attempt create an AuditRecord?
options: Create a system-actor record with no actor ID for every failed login.
Create a staff-actor record only when an account can be resolved, and no record for an unknown email.
Represent every attempt with another identity or target-account convention that State 1 must define.
open_points.default_guess: Record every failed login with `actor_kind=system`, no actor ID, and no reason code.

events: An unauthenticated caller attempts staff login with that email and an arbitrary password.
outcomes: The portal creates one `staff.login_failed` AuditRecord using the system actor.
The portal creates no record because no required staff `actor_id` exists.
witness.observer: An administrator or audit reader sees a different failed-login history.

open_points.subject: ProjectOverview project availability
open_points.text: The declared DTO requires `project: ProjectContext`, but the carried change says “the project context is absent ... and a `project_availability` says so, like the other five pairs.”
open_points.question: Does ProjectOverview have a nullable `project` plus `project_availability`, or is `project` always required and a post-guard context-read failure still fails the overview?
options: Add `project_availability: ViewAvailability` and make `project` present exactly when available.
Keep required `project: ProjectContext` and fail the overview when the context read fails.
open_points.default_guess: Use the carried change: add the availability pair and allow project context to be absent.

witness.initial: The project guard has successfully validated active project P.
events: The overview builder performs the later Registry context read.
That context read fails because Registry times out, while the portal-owned overview components remain readable.
outcomes: The caller receives a partial ProjectOverview with absent `project` and `project_availability=temporarily_unavailable`.
The declared DTO cannot represent that result, so the whole overview fails or an invented ProjectContext must be supplied.
witness.observer: The overview caller sees either partial data or an operation failure.
